conventions: Where a negative existential אַיִן, or a possessive or obligation לְ, is the morpheme that makes the clause existential, possessive or modal, the whole English frame the ASV writes in the copula's place belongs to that morpheme's unit — including a modal or auxiliary written inside it — and the unit heads on the negation word or on the relational word, while a dependent infinitive keeps only its own written לְ and its lexical verb. 20.6 `אֵין ... לְהִתְיַצֵּב` gives *none is able* to אַיִן, *to* to the לְ and *withstand* to the infinitive; 20.12 `אֵין בָּנוּ כֹּחַ` gives *have no* to אַיִן, *we* to the suffix and *might* to the noun; 20.17 `לֹא לָכֶם לְהִלָּחֵם` gives *shall ... need* to the לְ, *Ye* to its suffix and *fight* to the infinitive; 20.25 `לְאֵין מַשָּׂא` gives *more than they could* to אַיִן and *carry away* to the noun. What decides it is that the frame states the existence, possession or obligation the Hebrew predicates by that one morpheme, and that giving it to the infinitive would leave one Hebrew verb holding two English predications. The competing reading, which gives the modal to the infinitive under rules 48 and 52, is named in each unit's note.

The ASV spells some single English words as two target tokens: *To morrow* for מָחָר at 20.16 and 20.17, *watch tower* for מִצְפֶּה at 20.24. Both tokens belong to the one source noun's unit and the head goes by rule 31's subtraction to the token carrying the lexeme — *morrow* in the first, *watch* in the second, the two falling on opposite sides because the test is run on the words and not on their order. The opening *To* of *To morrow* is not a preposition supplied for an adverbial accusative under rule 33 and is never `added`, even though מָחָר is an adverbial accusative of time and the word stands exactly where such a supplied preposition would stand.
report: Read all 80 candidate groups and the full verse dump end to end. The table is blind to `added` units, so the chapter's six were checked separately (v2 *some*, v4 *help*, v11 *how*, v18 *his* twice, v23 *them*): each is a supplied subject noun, object noun, object pronoun or possessive with no morpheme in its clause to answer for it, and no comparable supplied word is folded into a neighbouring unit elsewhere in the chapter.

No cross-verse split found. The large buckets are the ASV rendering one morpheme differently in different contexts: וְ takes whatever connective the ASV wrote and is unrepresented in the four places it wrote none (11, 21, 24, 25 — three of them apodosis waws); לְ before an infinitive is aligned wherever a word is written and unrepresented wherever the recasting writes none (rule 52's own count); מִן, עַל, בְּ, אֶל and עִם each take the ASV's word.

Construct-chain determiners were the one place worth re-deriving, because 20.16 carries a recorded correction. The chapter counts consistently: an anarthrous rectum fronts the article's *the* to the phrase's left edge (מַעֲלֵה הַצִּיץ → *the ascent of Ziz*), an arthrous one writes a *the* before each word and neither is fronted (סוֹף הַנַּחַל, מַמְלְכוֹת הַגּוֹיִם 20.6, מַמְלְכוֹת הָאֲרָצוֹת 20.29, בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִים 20.19, תּוֹךְ הַקָּהָל 20.14), and a rectum carrying a demonstrative leaves every article unrepresented (20.7, 20.9 twice, 20.12, 20.15, 20.26). Both shapes stand in 20.16 and the verse's own notes say why.

Coordinated members are counted the same way in both directions and are not a split: 20.22 writes one בְ and two *to*s, so the second *to* is the one preposition's distributed scope (rule 25); 20.23 writes two לְs and one *to*, and 20.28 three בְּs and one *with*, so the later morphemes are unrepresented (rules 22, 40). 20.25's three waws answer to three written connectives (*both*, *and*, *and*) one to one, so no correlative pair arises.

הֲ takes the fronted question auxiliary in all three of its occurrences (20.6 *art*, 20.7 *Didst*, 20.12 *wilt*), and 20.6's second *art* and second *not* are the distributed scope of the single הֲ and לֹא under rule 25. אַיִן heads on its negation word in all four occurrences (20.6, 20.12, 20.24, 20.25); the frame family is recorded as a convention.

BSB: no genuine error among the disagreements. The R×23 and Td×18 blocks are the documented convention difference — prepositions this project marks unrepresented where the ASV's recasting writes no word for the relation (rule 40), the לְ of לֵאמֹר (rule 27), preposition-plus-construct fusions (rule 30), and agreement or demonstrative-displaced articles (rules 41, 47). The individual items are the same conventions: 20.6 הוּא is the resuming pronoun of a tripartite clause whose copula the interrogative particle took (rules 20, 22); 20.10 בָהֶם and 20.14 עָלָיו are resumptive elements the ASV renders once; 20.23 רֵעֵהוּ's suffix is unwritten inside *another*; the two To markers are rule 16's ordinary case. Nothing here would be changed without worsening the alignment.

No promotion. The modal-frame family (20.6, 20.12, 20.17, 20.25) is the only judgment that reaches beyond a rule already in the contract, but two of its four units are hedged against the competing rule-48/52 reading and the corpus extract supplied here carries no אַיִן or possessive-לְ counts to weigh it against, so it is recorded as a convention rather than written into the contract.
